Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturers use it as a flavoring and acidulant component in oral preparations, where botanical sourcing is a label or regulatory requirement for the industry. Cosmetic formulators also include it in scalp-care and anti-blemish product lines to meet consumer demand for recognized herbal ingredients. Its recognized status in flavoring applications makes it relevant. This extract is useful for suppliers sourcing botanical extracts for functional personal care products with flavor-masking or sensory modification needs. It is typically supplied as a liquid extract or dry powder. Standard offerings include hydroglycolic and hydroalcoholic extract forms suited to cosmetic and topical pharmaceutical use.
